version.changelog:
- Major refactor: streamlined to a compact core (~200 lines), merging simplicity and core features.
- Added automatic local model detection (Ollama, LM Studio); cloud model registry built-in.
- Core CLI and Python API redesigned for simplicity—easy model listing, routing, and status checks.
- Sensitive data detection improved; privacy mode forces use of local models for secure requests.
- Centralized configuration now optional; auto-detects setup if no models.json present.
- Legacy scripts, references, and excess code removed for easier maintenance.

llm.summary: The skill's code mostly matches its stated purpose (routing between local and cloud models with privacy detection), but multiple documentation vs. code inconsistencies and a few surprising behaviors (overbroad privacy matching, on-disk context persistence) mean you should review or test it before installing.

dimensions.detail: The code implements model routing, local Ollama detection, a built-in cloud registry, complexity scoring, and privacy detection — which aligns with the description. However the SKILL.md claims LM Studio auto-detection but the detector only reads Ollama configs. The README/CLI paths reference core/ and modules/ directories, yet the packaged files live under skill/*. These mismatches suggest packaging or documentation errors.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions (SKILL.md) reference paths like python3 skill/core/router.py and modules/detector.py that don't match the included files (skill/router.py, skill/detector.py, skill/context.py). If used as-is the examples/imports may fail. The privacy detection is implemented via regexes that will mark emails and many API-like patterns as 'sensitive' and force local routing — this is functionally coherent with the stated privacy goal but is fairly broad and may trigger on benign input. Context tracking persists truncated message content to ~/.model-router/contexts.json which stores user content on disk (possible sensitive data persistence).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or external downloads are included (instruction-only install), and code contains no outbound network calls or subprocess usage. That reduces supply-chain risk. The package includes Python source only; there is no installer that fetches remote code.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables and does not attempt to read unrelated secrets. A fallback model entry references api_key_env metadata (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) but that is just metadata — the skill does not demand credentials at install time. It does read a local Ollama config path (~/.ollama/models.json) and writes configuration/context files under ~/.model-router — these accesses are proportionate to its purpose but are noteworthy because they persist data on disk.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no special privileges. The skill creates and writes its own config directory (~/.model-router/) and contexts.json for conversation history; it does not modify other skills or system-wide settings. Persisting conversation snippets on disk is expected for context tracking but is a privacy consideration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
What to watch for before installing or using this skill:
- Documentation vs. code mismatch: SKILL.md examples and import paths (core/, modules/) do not match the included files (skill/...). This likely means the provided examples will fail unless the package is repackaged; ask the author for corrected packaging or test in a safe sandbox.
- LM Studio claim: The docs claim auto-detect for Ollama and LM Studio, but detector only reads Ollama config files — don't rely on LM Studio detection unless code is updated.
- Privacy behavior: The privacy regexes will treat emails and many API-like tokens as sensitive and will force routing to the primary (local) model. That protects data but can be overzealous; expect false positives.
- On-disk persistence: Conversation history (truncated messages) is stored in ~/.model-router/contexts.json. If you handle sensitive data, review or disable context tracking, or secure that file.
- No network/exfil signs found in the code, and no install-time downloads are used — lower supply-chain risk — but the packaging/import mismatches mean the runtime behavior might differ from the docs.
Recommended actions: run the code in a confined environment first, inspect or run unit tests to verify imports work, review the contexts.json contents after a test run, and ask the maintainer to fix the documentation/import/package layout and to clarify LM Studio support. If you need to be strict about privacy, verify that 'primary' truly maps to an offline/local model on your machine before sending any secrets.
